amount.value: 27.49% variable APR, based on creditworthiness and varying with the market based on the Prime Rate

trigger.value: Applies to balances on purchases. You can avoid interest on purchases by paying your entire balance by the due date each month (a grace period of at least 25 days); lose the grace period by paying less than the full balance and interest accrues from the transaction date.

plain_language_warning.value: Carrying a purchase balance costs about 27.49% a year, and the rate floats with the Prime Rate so it can climb. You only avoid this interest if you pay the statement in full every month; pay even a dollar short and interest starts from the purchase date.

plain_language_warning.value: Cash advances cost about 28.49% a year, higher than the purchase rate, and interest starts the moment you take the cash with no grace period. The variable rate can rise with the Prime Rate.

amount.value: Cash Loans, ATM Loans, and Convenience Check Loans: either $10 or up to 5% of the amount of each advance, whichever is greater. Cash Equivalent Transactions: either $10 or 5% of the amount of each advance, whichever is greater.

trigger.value: Charged each time you take a cash advance, including cash or ATM withdrawals, convenience checks, and cash-equivalent purchases (such as money orders, gift cards, wire transfers, or gambling chips). The fee is treated as a cash advance and accrues interest at the cash advance APR from the transaction date.

plain_language_warning.value: Every cash advance adds at least $10, or 5% of the amount if that is larger, on top of the higher 28.49% cash advance rate that starts accruing immediately. Note that money orders, gift cards, and similar cash-equivalent buys count as cash advances too.
